commands.command: scripts/test-in-lima.sh bash -c 'source scripts/eip-lanes.sh; eip_warm; eip_lane us-iis-05'

diagnostic:
S2 GREEN: the us-iis-05 lane is 20/20 and the whole instance-integration-setup lane 96/96, with check-arch and xtask smoke green. Another Slack app submitted while a workspace is connected through the app in effect now waits on its own page until the same admin confirms it, also when the current app is the environment's.

The gate is SubmissionDoor::of(kind, connected) in handlers/instance.rs (L3): NewApp with 1 or more connected workspaces waits, a Rotate and a NewApp with nobody connected are saved at once by the shipped save path, so the S1 doors are untouched. The count is Store::connected_slack_workspaces, one read over integration_connections with kind slack and a state other than disconnected, counted by distinct workspace_id (D10, CreateNew as designed); a count the store cannot answer never reads as none connected (B1) - the save door answers the page and nothing is held. confirm_lines carries I-14's n = 1 and counted forms verbatim over the client ID in effect, which is app_in_effect's answer, so I-6/I-7 and the gate read one app (D3).

A held submission is plan_hold_pending in slack_app.rs - the same sealing as plan_replace into the pending row's own slots, now sharing seal_both and fence with it - stored by Store::hold_pending_slack_app: the shared lock, the seal fence, the upsert, no activity line and no version bump, because nothing a reader sees changed (K8, ADR-IIS-004 r2). Migration 0034 holds the single-row table with its 10-minute expiry, written from the injected clock; PENDING_HELD_FOR owns the ten minutes in slack_app.rs beside the sealing.

DESIGN defect found and repaired within the design's own rule, not around it: the confirm cannot copy the held sealed bytes into instance_slack_app, because a sealed value is bound to the row it is stored in (ADR-EIP-004 row-bound AAD) - the first lane run stored unopenable bytes and three scenarios read I-13. Store::apply_pending_slack_app now takes the caller's re-seal closure and the fence key id, exactly as the shipped store_secrets_key takes its Resealer: the store reads the row under the exclusive lock, decides requester and expiry (PendingSlackApp::applicable_by), hands the held bytes to slack_app::reseal_held_for_save, deletes the row and ends in the one fenced save_slack_app, which both the admin's save and the confirm now share as the single writer of instance_slack_app (reuse obligation honoured; check_arch's seal-fence list gains hold_pending_slack_app only). PendingApplied gained Refused(E) for that closure, as SecretsKeyOutcome has. Every Slack sealing and opening still happens in slack_app.rs.

The pending secrets join the seal fence, reseal_sealed_values and the boot probe's sealed_values; credential_values (connections plus the saved app) now feeds direct_seals alone, so the held app is no I-22 credential (D5) and Resealed keeps it out of the count. The hourly retention tick prunes a row at or past its expiry through the one instance-write capability (four methods added: hold, apply, count, prune); the expiry instant itself is already too late, which the L4 table reads at at(10).

Finite tables authored at the locators the S2 acceptance rows cite: handlers/instance.rs the_count_forms_i14_and_i15_read_and_the_gate_the_connected_count_decides (L3 gate over 0/1/2/3/137 for both kinds, L11's I-14 forms), handlers/instance.rs the_table_of_what_the_confirm_and_remove_pages_reach_when_they_are_only_read (L6: ReadOnlyDoor::SlackConfirm's reads, a PageRead list with no write variant in the type, which the GET handler itself follows), and crates/foundry-store/tests/iis_instance_store.rs the_finite_table_of_when_a_held_slack_app_may_still_be_applied (L4/F188 over the holder at +1 and +9, the expiry instant, +11, another admin, the second confirm, nothing held, plus the prune fencepost and the hold writing the pending row alone). I-15's forms and the remove page's row are left to the slice that delivers that door (P4/S3): asserting them now would be vacuous.

No oracle, support or feature record was edited. No refactor commit was needed: seal_both/fence in slack_app.rs are extracted with their second caller, not as a standalone behaviour-preserving move. One shipped unit test double (worker.rs retention_tests) gained the new capability methods to keep compiling, with its assertions untouched.
